property_summary: Only the current owner can successfully change the owner; the bug allows any address to call transferOwnership and change the owner.

For any caller address, if transferOwnership is called, the resulting owner must either stay the same (if msg.sender is not the current owner) or change to the new owner (if msg.sender is the current owner); the bug version always changes the owner regardless of the caller.

For any caller, a call to transferOwnership must either revert (if caller is not the current owner) or succeed and update owner to the new address (if caller is the owner); the bug allows any caller to update owner without reverting.
Any address that is not the current owner cannot change the owner via transferOwnership; the bug lets any caller (non-owner) change it.

For any caller, if transferOwnership is called and does not revert, the new owner must equal the argument; the bug allows a non-owner caller to succeed but may set the owner to a different address than expected.
Only the current owner can change the owner; the bug allows any caller to change it.
After any transferOwnership call, the owner must equal the new owner argument; the buggy version never updates owner, so a subsequent call with a different address breaks this rule.

After a successful transferOwnership call, calling the owned() modifier should not revert; the buggy version deletes the assignment so owned() still reverts for the original owner unless they already own.

After a successful transferOwnership, the owner must equal the new owner argument; the buggy version never updates owner, so a subsequent call to transferOwnership with a different address followed by a query of owner reveals the original owner was not changed.

After a successful transferOwnership call, the owner must equal the new owner argument; the buggy version never updates owner, so a subsequent call from the intended new owner reverts on the onlyOwner modifier.

After transferOwnership is called, the new owner must equal the _newOwner argument; the bug sets owner to msg.sender instead, so a call by a non-_newOwner address makes owner different from _newOwner.

After calling transferOwnership by the current owner, the address returned by the public owner() getter must be the _newOwner argument; the bug sets it to msg.sender instead, so when msg.sender != _newOwner the returned owner mismatches _newOwner.

For any initial owner and any new owner candidates, a call to transferOwnership by the current owner must set owner to the explicitly provided _newOwner; the bug sets it to msg.sender instead, so for any msg.sender that differs from _newOwner the owner() will not match _newOwner.

After a successful call to transferOwnership by the current owner, ownership must transfer to the _newOwner argument; the bug sets owner to msg.sender instead, so when msg.sender != _newOwner the resulting owner fails to match _newOwner.

After the current owner calls transferOwnership with any _newOwner, owner must equal _newOwner; the bug sets owner to msg.sender instead, so any call where msg.sender != _newOwner makes owner mismatch _newOwner.
For any caller and any valid owner, a call to owned() from the owner does not revert in the reference, but always reverts in the mutant.
For any owner, calling owned() succeeds (does not revert); the buggy version with require(false) always reverts.

For any caller address, calling owned() should succeed (not revert) when msg.sender equals owner, and should revert when msg.sender does not equal owner; the bug reverses this by requiring msg.sender != owner, making it revert for the owner and succeed for non-owners.
For any fuzzed address caller, calling owned() succeeds if and only if caller equals owner; the bug reverses this, making owned() fail for the owner and succeed for non-owners.

For any caller, transferOwnership with a valid non-null input argument must always succeed and update the 'owner' state variable, but the bug's `onlyOwner` modifier requires msg.sender == address(0), so no caller can ever change the owner, leaving it permanently unset.
For any caller that is the current owner, transferOwnership to a non-zero new owner must succeed and update the owner; the bug version's modifier always fails, so the owner never changes.

For any initial owner set by the setup, calling transferOwnership from any address after pranking that address will succeed on the reference and fail on the mutant, because the mutant's modifier requires msg.sender == address(0) which no pranked call can satisfy.

For any caller and any new owner address, transferring ownership should succeed and update the owner, but the buggy modifier always requires msg.sender == address(0), so no valid caller can ever change the owner.
